class.name: AcousticMaterial
class.brief_description: How a surface treats sound that reaches it, for the Asosdot Acoustic Engine.
class.description: Give an [AcousticMaterial] to a collider's [member CollisionObject3D.acoustic_material] or [member CSGShape3D.acoustic_material], or to an [code]acoustic_material[/code] property of a script on a collider, and the [AcousticEngine] uses it for the sound that meets that collider. Colliders without one use [member ProjectSettings.audio/acoustics/default_material], and if that is empty, a material with the default values below. Some rough values: a concrete or brick wall lets through [code]0.01[/code] and absorbs [code]0.02[/code]; a plasterboard wall lets through [code]0.1[/code] and absorbs [code]0.1[/code]; a wooden door lets through [code]0.2[/code]; glass lets through [code]0.15[/code] and absorbs [code]0.05[/code]; carpet absorbs [code]0.3[/code]; a heavy curtain lets through [code]0.5[/code] and absorbs [code]0.6[/code].

members.member: How much of the sound that hits the surface is soaked up rather than reflected, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. Rooms with absorbent surfaces have a shorter, duller reverb.

How much of the sound the surface reflects is spread in every direction rather than bounced like a mirror, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. Rough and cluttered surfaces scatter more, which spreads the reverb wider.

How much of the sound goes through the surface to the other side, from [code]0.0[/code] for nothing to [code]1.0[/code] for all of it. A sound that goes through several surfaces keeps what each lets through, one after another, and loses its high end first.
